gacc_sections.narrative: Kartar, Colville Agency, BIA. Fifteen miles southeast of Omak, WA. Grass, timber and brush. Moderate fire behavior with backing and running. Structures threatened. Area and road closures in effect. Upriver, Northeast Region, Washington DNR. Started on private land one mile east of Spokane, WA. Timber and grass. Minimal fire behavior with smoldering. Numerous residences threatened. Evacuations, area, road and trail closures in effect. Tule Rd, Yakama Agency, BIA. CIMT (NW Team 2). CIMT is also managing the Roza incident. Five miles south of Toppenish, WA. Grass, brush and dormant brush. Minimal fire behavior with creeping and smoldering. Residences threatened. Area closures in effect. Roza, Spokane District, BLM. Nine miles north of Selah, WA. Brush and grass. Minimal fire behavior with smoldering. Area closures in effect. Reduction in acreage due to more accurate mapping. Old Emigrant, Pendleton Unit, Oregon DOF. Six miles southeast of Pendleton, OR. Grass and brush. Minimal fire behavior with smoldering and creeping. Residences threatened. Road closures in effect. Reduction in acreage due to more accurate mapping. Tucannon Mutual Aid, Washington State Fire Marshal's Office. Eight miles east of Dayton, WA. Grass and brush. Minimal fire behavior with smoldering. Residences threatened. Last report unless significant activity occurs.

Sawmill, Color Country Paria Unit, BLM. Forty-four miles northwest of Cedar City, UT. Dormant brush and grass. Extreme fire behavior with running, torching and spotting. Structures threatened. Dellenbaugh, Lake Mead National Recreation Area, NPS. Eighty miles south of St. George, UT. Timber. Minimal fire behavior with creeping and torching. Residences threatened.

Structures and energy infrastructure threatened. Area and road closures in effect. Reduction in acreage due to more accurate mapping. Rio, Santa Fe NF, USFS. Fifteen miles east of Espanola, NM. Timber, brush and grass. Moderate fire behavior with backing, creeping and smoldering. Bear, Gila NF, USFS. Eighteen miles southeast of Quemado, NM. Timber and brush. predictive_services_discussion: Scattered dry thunderstorms will focus a bit farther to the east today, sparking an uptick in new ignitions across much of southern Idaho, northeastern Nevada and far northern Utah. Thunderstorms will be more isolated with westward extent into northern California and southeastern Oregon. Critical fire weather with relative humidity as low as 5-15% and west-southwest wind gusts from 30-45 mph will stretch from western Wyoming into northern parts of the West Slope and much of eastern and southern Utah. Farther to the south, from the Four Corners into western Arizona, a critical burn environment will take shape due to the combination of hot temperatures, relative humidity in the single digits and gusty southwesterly winds. Westerly Cascade gap winds will increase across eastern Washington and Oregon, potentially affecting any of the active fires in the Northwest. Hot and unstable conditions, along with scattered afternoon thunderstorms will continue across the Florida peninsula. Look for severe thunderstorms and areas of significant flash flooding from eastern Colorado through portions of the Missouri Valley. The potential for lightning-ignited fires will also increase across central and eastern Interior Alaska as thunderstorms become more numerous and temperatures continue to trend higher. Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands will see another hot day, with dry trade winds maintaining an elevated risk for fire activity.
